hypothesis: Post-09:30 EMA pullback shorts are dominated by false reversals driven by microstructure noise (transaction-price bounce/indecision) rather than genuine supply-driven reversal. Requiring that the alert candle be a decisive reversal bar—operationalized as real-body dominance (high body_pct) and/or low wick share—will restore a tradable subset of post-09:30 entries (trade_count_non0930 > 0) and improve their median_expectancy versus an unfiltered post-09:30 cohort, while keeping the strong 09:30 edge intact.
mechanism: Microstructure research shows observed short-horizon reversals can be mechanically induced by bid–ask effects even when efficient value is unchanged. A candle with large wicks and small body near the EMA is consistent with two-sided probing/noise and is more likely to be adversely selected for a break-of-extreme entry. Implement an alert-candle geometry confirmation for shorts in entry buckets excluding 09:30: only arm/keep the alert if the alert candle’s body is sufficiently large relative to its range (or equivalently wick share is sufficiently small). This confirmation is computed at alert-arming time from the alert bar’s OHLC (already produced in strategy feature arrays) and does not merge timeframes.
dimension_novelty: Prior signal-quality work in this job focused on alert_close vs EMA confirmation (which currently rejects essentially all post-09:30 candidates) and attempted close-location filters that were blocked/obscured by diagnostics aggregation issues. This thesis tests a distinct mechanism family: filtering microstructure-noise/bid–ask-bounce-like reversals by requiring the alert candle to be a decisive reversal bar (large real body relative to range, or equivalently low combined wick share), which is not a nearby threshold tweak of the EMA-side rule and can pass a meaningful subset of post-09:30 setups.
underexplored_dimensions_considered: regime_conditioning (symbol-day early raw_setup gate as a day-type classifier)
exit_mechanism (adjust trailing activation/timeout to better match early right-tail behavior)
novel_connection: Connects microstructure literature on transaction-price reversal artifacts (bid–ask bounce / return-computation bias) to a directly testable bar-structure discriminator (body dominance / wick share) that should preferentially reject ‘noisy’ EMA touches while keeping true rejection/acceptance independent from the close-vs-EMA sign test that currently collapses trade_count after 09:30.
orthogonality_defense: Unlike require_alert_close_below_ema_for_non0930_shorts, this does not gate on EMA-side at the close (which has been shown to reject 35,887 post-09:30 candidates and produce 0 post-09:30 trades). Unlike the prior close-location attempt, this uses a different candle-geometry definition tied to microstructure bounce/indecision (body vs wick dominance) and is intended to be permissive enough to restore some post-09:30 trading while still filtering low-quality signals.
falsification_or_alternative: If post-09:30 trades remain unprofitable even when restricted to high-body/low-wick alert candles (N>=200), then the failure mode is likely not microstructure bounce but a broader regime shift (information-driven continuation). In that case, a regime_conditioning gate (e.g., symbol-day early raw_setup presence) would be a more plausible next lever than any candle-geometry filter.
evidence: Web: Roll (1984) demonstrates bid–ask bounce induces negative serial dependence in transaction-price changes (mechanical ‘reversal’), motivating filters that avoid indecisive/bounce-like bars. https://www.acsu.buffalo.edu/~keechung/MGF743/Readings/Roll%201984.pdf

Web: Blume & Stambaugh (1983) show transaction-price-based returns can be biased by bid–ask effects, implying that naive reversal signals can be spurious without structure confirmation. https://www-2.rotman.utoronto.ca/~kan/3032/pdf/BiasInReturns/Blume_Stambaugh_JFE_1983.pdf

Data (job-26 best run): alert_close_above_ema_reject accounts for 35,887 of 35,908 rejected_signal events and occurs entirely on/after 09:35, causing post-09:30 trade_count=0; we need a less binary confirmation that can preserve some post-09:30 flow while still targeting low-quality reversals.

expected_effects.rationale: Filtering out indecisive/bounce-like alert candles should reduce stop-outs/adverse selection in post-09:30 entries, improving aggregate PF without sacrificing the core 09:30 cohort.
Relative to the current best (which yields 0 post-09:30 trades), this geometry filter should be permissive enough to restore some post-09:30 trades while leaving 09:30 excluded from filtering.

requested_primitives: engine primitive to compute alert candle body_pct (abs(close-open)/(high-low)) and apply as a rejection rule at alert-arming time, bucket-scoped via apply_to_entry_buckets_excluding
why_not_overfit: This is not a tuned cutoff on time or stop distance; it is a structural filter derived from a known microstructure artifact (bounce/indecision). The prediction is falsifiable on large event counts by comparing pass/fail cohorts (geometry-pass vs geometry-fail) within the same entry buckets, and it should generalize because wick/body dominance is a stable descriptor of auction-to-continuous noise vs decisive reversal behavior.
